newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on weak peso, jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on weak peso, jitters.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended up 65 basis points at 22.90 percent on Thursday under pressure from a weak peso and jitters in the run up to key U.S. economic data, traders said.
"Pressure came mainly from the slide in the peso and uncertainty ahead of U.S. employment data due out tomorrow," a dealer said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had closed three centavos weaker at 7.9590/7.9610 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended up 45 basis points at 25.00 percent.
Another trader said the market was "most uncertain" and had already begun to act on an expected additional hike in U.S. interest rates at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting, on May 21.

"Rates have been trending upwards in Mexico as the FOMC hike (in U.S. interest rates on March 25) is equivalent to a rise of 150-200 basis points here, and above all because dealers expect further hikes in future," he said.
Other traders said the market had been "very speculative" due to brokers left holding large positions in money market paper.

"There were a lot of trades settled at low rates in Easter week, since when rates have gained almost 200 basis points, so many have been holding paper and waiting for rates to fall so as not to post losses," one trader said.
Dealers noted overnight Cetes rates had at one stage been as high as 23.70 pesos.
Banco de Mexico drained 1.919 billion pesos to offset surplus liquidity in the market, through three secondary auctions which it assigned at between 25.19-25.22 percent.
Liquidity of 2.289 billion pesos was slated to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
